Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short packet and a partially completed SIG worksheet; below are the paste-ready lines and the key differences you requested. If you want, I can convert these into the SIG XML answers as well.

Quick paste-ready descriptions (1–2 sentences each):
- Hosted: Redwood-hosted inference endpoints that run on shared infrastructure managed by Redwood. Designed for fastest time-to-value; customer data is isolated in per-tenant logical partitions and encrypted in transit and at rest.
- Dedicated: Customer-dedicated GPU pools managed by Redwood with reserved capacity and tenant-level isolation; ideal for predictable throughput and stricter tenancy controls while still under Redwood operational management.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer-deployed control plane and/or on-prem inference nodes under the customer's network boundaries (VPC, air-gapped), with customer-managed infrastructure and optional air-gapped installer for regulated environments.

Key differences — bullets for SIG entries:
- Data residency: Hosted: region-based tenancy (Redwood-managed regions); Dedicated: can be pinned to region/zone per contract; Private: fully customer-controlled location (VPC or on-prem).
- Network isolation: Hosted: logical tenant isolation + TLS; Dedicated: network segmentation between tenants with optional private network peering; Private: runs inside customer network (no public egress required).
- KMS/HSM / keys: Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS with customer key import available on request; Dedicated: bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options and customer KMS integrations available; Private: customer-managed KMS/HSM — keys never leave customer environment unless explicitly configured.
- Audit logs & access: Hosted: standard retention and access via Console / API; Dedicated: extended retention and dedicated access logs; Private: logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM and retained per customer policy; audit trail available for on-prem agents.

Attachments included: SIG_worksheet_filled.xlsx (partial), redwood_deployment_appendix.pdf (one-page summary), network_diagram.png (high-level).

I'll loop in Karthik for the technical KMS/HSM wording in the SIG. If you need a compact one-paragraph table for the SIG, say the word and I'll produce it.

Best,

Diego / Sarah — adding a technical clarification for the SIG answers around cryptography and network controls. Paste these as short bullets under the relevant SIG questions (cryptography / network):

- Hosted (Redwood-managed): Customer data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest using AES-256. Root keys are managed by Redwood KMS; we support importing customer root keys via a secure import flow. HSM-backed key storage is available for customers under enterprise contracts (key material stored in HSM within Redwood cloud providers).

- Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra, customer-dedicated pools): All storage and ephemeral caches are AES-256 at rest; customers may configure BYOK where Redwood stores only wrapped keys and does not have direct plaintext key access. Network ACLs and private peering options restrict administrative access; we provide dedicated audit streams for admin actions.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): Keys and key lifecycle are fully controlled by the customer; if an on-prem installer is used, the deployment can be configured such that no organization-level telemetry leaves the environment. For SIG evidence, provide a statement that the deployment is configured with customer KMS and indicate if the HSM module is used.

Also: for the SIG item about "who has access to raw model inputs", include that Redwood engineers may access debug traces only when explicitly allowed (customer-controlled access window) and on Dedicated/Hosted environments such access is governed by access control policies and logged. For Private, access is controlled by customer admin.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
